newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker with bonds ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker with bonds ahead of data.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished weaker on Thursday, depressed by sagging bonds as nervous investors awaited Friday's Canadian and U.S. inflation data.
The TSE 300 Composite Index dropped 27.52 points to close at 5136.25 in heavy volume of 89.2 million shares valued at C$1.25 billion.

Declining stocks easily outpaced advances 531 to 347 with 281 issues ending flat. "The market is very sensitive to economic data, particularly numbers that could affect interest rates," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor with Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.
The U.S. non-farm payrolls report for August is considered a key measure of U.S. economic growth. Katzin said some investors were worried that a strong number could result in higher interest rates.
Canada's August labor force survey is also due on Friday.
All but one of Toronto's 14 sub-groups ended the day on the weak side.
Gold, financial services, conglomerates and transportation posted the heaviest losses. The only bright spot was consumer products, which gained 44 points.
* Seagram Co Ltd pushed the consumer product group higher, finishing up 0.80 at 46. The entertaining and beverage giant reported improved second-quarter results earlier today.

* Forestry products giant Domtar Inc topped active stocks, rising 0.10 to 11.30 on 4.3 million shares. Traders said the heavy action was linked to the redemption of the company's convertible debentures, but takeover rumors were also swirling around the Quebec-based pulp and paper firm.
* Among weak stocks, Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc lost 2.70 to 98.50. A U.S. brokerage earlier today downgraded Potash Corp's merger target Arcadian Corp.
